newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher on high volume.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher on high volume.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on Thursday on their highest volume in more than three years dominated by Maof options speculators, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.32 percent, or 3.93 points, to 301.25 on very high all-share turnover of 318 million shekels against 176 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.49 percent higher at 308.71.

"The session opened with a real war between options speculators. Volume in the Meretz session (the preliminary computerised session in which the index for the June contracts was fixed) was a very high 198 million shekels with most of it concentrated in the Maof shares," said Michael Politzer, head of the economics department at the Central Securities Corp.
"Some players were trying to push the Maof down to 300 while others where trying to bring it to 305," Politzer said.

Daniella Finn, head of sales at Ilanot Batucha, said that after the expiry of the Maof options the market continued rising. "The momentum from the Meretz continued and the market rose across the board."
Finn said that the market was gaining confidence from the budget cut and talks with the Palestinians.
The Israeli cabinet approved on Wednesday a 800 million shekel cut in the 1997 budget. The cuts were the third round of budget slashing since the draft 1997 budget was presented last autumn.
"The market is very strong and investors are not interested in negative news. There is no clear reason why it should start falling in the near term," Politzer said.

Politzer added that as long as bond yields continue to decline and inflation remains under control the market will continue to rise. "The government continues to cut the budget, privatisation goes on and the bond market is rising. The economy looks good," he said.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi which rose 1.0 percent to 577 agorot on volume of 24.4 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which gained 0.75 percent to 787 on turnover of 23 million shekels; and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which rose 1.0 to 1,003 agorot on turnover of 21.3 million shekels.
